### 7.5 The second opt-out, mapped — the report collector's application half

**Section [7.1](#71-the-policy)'s opt-out list is closed at two endpoints, and only one of them was
specified anywhere in this document.** `POST /Home/Error` is section
[8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types)'s. `POST /csp-report` had a filter attribute, a
justification and a coverage row — and **no action, no request model, no parser, no limiter registration
and no position in the pipeline.** A closed list that names an endpoint the composition root does not
contain is a list with a hole in it, so this section closes it.

**The division of labour is unchanged: [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns what the
endpoint must *do*** — the two accepted content types, the two report shapes and their field naming, the
per-field allow-lists, re-serialization, length and character bounds, the numeric caps, the origin check,
the phase, the promotion criteria and the daily review. None of that is restated here. What this section
owns is the other half: **where the code sits, what registers it, and where in the pipeline it runs**.
The endpoint is **permanent**, not part of the report-only phase: that subsection retires the report-only
*disposition* on day 14 and keeps the endpoint, its caps and its review.

**What is added, and what is not.**

| Element | Where it sits | Why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The action | `CspReport()` on **`HomeController`**, attribute-routed | AAP §0.4.1's map names exactly **six** controllers and this document does not add a seventh. `HomeController` already owns the *other* opt-out, `/Home/Error` (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types)), so section [7.1](#71-the-policy)'s closed list becomes **two actions in one file** — one place to read, and one place for row 40 of section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) to be checked against |
| The request models | **`Binding/CspReportModels.cs`** — a new file in the folder `Binding/CheckoutInputModel.cs` (section [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine)) already occupies | [04 §12.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s map delegates the file-by-file contents of `Binding/` and `Services/` to this document, so a file here changes no project, no folder set and no project graph. They are deserialization targets carrying `[JsonPropertyName]` attributes, which is what `Binding/` is for; nesting them privately inside the controller was rejected because the two shapes are a wire contract and a wire contract belongs beside the other one |
| The normalizer, the budgets and the emission | **`Services/CspReportSink.cs`**, registered as a **singleton** | The two hourly budgets are **process-wide mutable state** (below), so they cannot live in a per-request controller or a scoped service. Registered as the concrete type with no interface, on section [4.8](#48-the-service-layer-and-the-two-patterns-deliberately-not-adopted)'s stance: an abstraction with one implementation and one consumer buys a seam this suite does not use, because section [12.2](#122-the-architecture-http-level-black-box) tests through the endpoint |
| The rate-limit policy | `internal sealed class CspReportRateLimitPolicy : IRateLimiterPolicy<string>`, declared in **`Program.cs` after the last top-level statement**, beside the `public partial class Program` declaration stage 6's excerpt already puts there | `AddPolicy<TPartitionKey, TPolicy>` needs a **named type**, and the lambda overload that avoids one carries no per-policy rejection handler — `IRateLimiterPolicy<TPartitionKey>` declares both `GetPartition(HttpContext)` and `OnRejected` (API reference, ASP.NET Core 8), which is exactly the pair this endpoint needs. Declaring it in `Program.cs` keeps the composition and its policy in one file and adds none |
| What is **not** added | No project, no controller, no folder, no view, no configuration key beyond section [3.3](#33-the-target-configuration-contract)'s `Site:Hosts`, no database object, no migration, and **no global rate limiter** | A global limiter would silently throttle the catalog on behalf of an endpoint that receives diagnostic exhaust. One named policy, applied to one action, changes no other endpoint's behaviour |

**The action's declaration, attribute by attribute, because three of the five carry behaviour the
handler would otherwise have to hand-write.**

| Declaration | What it buys |
| --- | --- |
| `[HttpPost("/csp-report")]` | An **absolute** attribute route — the leading `/` is what keeps it from becoming `/Home/csp-report`, which is not the path [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s `Reporting-Endpoints` header and `report-uri` directive name. `POST` only: any other verb on this path is a 405, which stage 3 renders |
| `[AllowAnonymous]` | The caller is the browser's reporting machinery and can arrive with no session and no principal at all |
| `[IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]` | Section [7.1](#71-the-policy)'s row, and the mechanism its enumeration test asserts |
| `[Consumes("application/csp-report", "application/reports+json")]` | **415 for anything else, with the body unread** — [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s rule satisfied by framework metadata rather than by a hand-written check. `ConsumesAttribute` implements `IActionConstraint` **and** `IResourceFilter` (API reference, ASP.NET Core 8), and a resource filter runs before model binding, so an unsupported content type short-circuits before anything reads the request body |
| `[EnableRateLimiting("csp-report")]` | Attaches the one named policy below. It is the reason the middleware's position is a requirement rather than a preference (the official rule is quoted under stage 8) |
| `[RequestSizeLimit(65536)]` | The **64 KiB** ceiling of the larger media type. `RequestSizeLimitAttribute` "sets the request body size limit to the specified size" and carries `IRequestSizeLimitMetadata` (API reference, ASP.NET Core 8), so the ceiling is endpoint metadata rather than a server-wide change |

The **8 KiB** limit for `application/csp-report` cannot be a second attribute, because an attribute cannot
vary by the request's content type. It is the action's first statement: where the media type is the
smaller one, `IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature.MaxRequestBodySize` is set to `8 * 1024` — guarded on
`IsReadOnly`, because "if the app attempts to configure the limit on a request after it starts to read the
request, an exception is thrown" and that property is the documented way to check first (*Configure
options for the ASP.NET Core Kestrel web server*, .NET 8).

**Two mechanics decide whether those numbers are real, and one of them is the difference between a 413
and a 500.**

- **The declared length is checked before anything is read.** The action inspects
  `Request.ContentLength` first: absent, or above the cap for the request's media type, is answered
  **413** with no body and the stream untouched. That is what makes
  [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s "body never read" true rather than aspirational —
  the *server-side* limit is enforced during the read, not before it. A body-less length is treated as
  oversize rather than as a fourth status code, because a length the server cannot see cannot be bounded
  ahead of the read and a browser's report always declares one.
- **The server-side limit is the backstop for a lying `Content-Length`, and its exception must be caught
  locally.** Exceeding the limit mid-read raises `BadHttpRequestException`, and the status that reaches
  the client is **413** — verified on the pinned runtime by posting 20 000 bytes to an endpoint narrowed
  to 8 KiB, which answered `413 Payload Too Large` while the same request at 1 024 bytes answered 204.
  Left uncaught, that exception also travels the pipeline as an unhandled request failure into stage 2's
  handler and one `Error`-level record, which is precisely how a bounded body becomes the 500 and the
  alert storm [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) forbids. So the read is wrapped:
  `BadHttpRequestException` is answered 413, **every** other exception is counted and answered 204, and
  nothing escapes the action.

**The response set is three status codes, no body, and no cookie.**

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Accepted, or accepted-and-dropped by any of the field rules, the origin check or the budgets | **204**, no body |
| Rejected by the rate limiter | **204**, no body — set by the policy's `OnRejected` (below), so a rejection is indistinguishable from an acceptance and the endpoint is not a probe oracle |
| Body above the applicable cap, or no declared length | **413**, no body |
| Any other content type | **415**, no body, body unread |
| Anything at all going wrong inside | **204** and a counted drop. **Never 500**, never a redirect |

**It touches no session and no database, and one cost is stated rather than hidden.** The action reads no
session key, so stage 11 creates no session and no row in the distributed cache — otherwise every report
from every browser would mint one. It executes no query either, which is what
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s "no read of the database" requires. The honest cost:
`HomeController`'s constructor takes `MusicStoreEntities` (section
[4.1](#41-the-ten-manual-instantiation-sites-constructor-injection-replaces)), so a scoped context is
constructed and disposed on a report request. EF Core opens no connection until a query executes, so this
is a few allocations rather than a connection — and it is the price of keeping the two opt-outs in one
auditable file.

**What Stage 1 registers, and where the middleware goes.** Both are entered in section
[2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order), which stays the authoritative composition; they are named
here so the endpoint's contract is readable in one place.

| Registration | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `AddRateLimiter` | **One named policy, no global limiter.** `AddPolicy<string, CspReportRateLimitPolicy>("csp-report")` |
| `AddSingleton<CspReportSink>()` | The normalizer, the two hourly budgets and the emission |
| `UseRateLimiter()` | **Inside stage 8's group, immediately after `UseRouting()`.** The requirement is documented and not stylistic: "`UseRateLimiter` must be called after `UseRouting` when rate limiting endpoint specific APIs are used. For example, if the `[EnableRateLimiting]` attribute is used, `UseRateLimiter` must be called after `UseRouting`" (*Rate limiting middleware in ASP.NET Core*, .NET 8) — before routing, the endpoint's policy metadata has not been selected and the policy silently does not apply. Its order relative to `UseRequestTimeouts()` in that group does not matter; being **above stages 9 to 12** does, because it means a rejected report reaches neither authentication, nor session, nor the endpoint |

**The partition key is the address the ingress observed, and a caller cannot inflate it.**
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires partitioning on the client IP "as resolved
after forwarded-header processing — never on the socket address", and the mechanism is stage 1: the
forwarded-headers middleware rewrites `HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress`, so the policy reads that
property and gets the resolved value. `ForwardLimit = 1` (stage 1) is what makes it trustworthy — only
the entry the platform ingress appended is consumed, so a caller-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` value sits to
its left and is never read. Two consequences: the limiter's own partition table is bounded by **real**
client addresses rather than by strings a caller chooses, and a request arriving with no resolvable
forwarded address — which on either platform means it did not come through ingress — partitions under a
single fixed `unknown` key rather than creating one partition per caller.

The window is [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s: a **fixed window of 20 permits per 5
minutes**, `QueueLimit = 0` so a rejected request is refused immediately and never queued, and
`AutoReplenishment` on. Rejection writes **204** and no body from the policy's own `OnRejected` — which
is a deliberate override of a documented default rather than a bare assignment:
`RateLimiterOptions.RejectionStatusCode` "defaults to `Status503ServiceUnavailable`" and "will be set
before `OnRejected` is called, so any status code set by `OnRejected` will win over this default" (API
reference, ASP.NET Core 8). It is set **on the policy** rather than on the options object so that no
future rate-limited endpoint inherits a 204.

#### 7.5.1 Every limit is enforced per replica, so a "global" cap on an in-process limiter is not global

**This is the correction that changes two of [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s
numbers from a fleet quota into a per-replica budget.** The framework's rate limiter and any counter this
application keeps live in the worker process. [06 §3.5.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) fixes
autoscale at **floor 2, ceiling 6**, so there are always at least two of everything and never more
than six — and affinity ([06 §8.3](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)) cannot be leaned on, both
because it is being retired and because a browser's report is sent by the reporting machinery rather than
by the page. A cap described as "across all clients" and implemented in one process is therefore
multiplied by the instance count unless the number is divided first.

| [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s figure | What a replica enforces | Fleet-wide worst case at the ceiling of six |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-client rate — 20 requests per 5-minute window | **20 per 5 minutes, unchanged** | 120 per 5 minutes for one client — 0.4 requests per second against an endpoint that answers 204 with no body under an 8 KiB cap |
| Accepted-report volume — 2 000 per hour | **333 per hour** | **1 998 per hour** — at or below the stated figure |
| Distinct `blocked-uri` cardinality — 200 per hour | **33 per hour** | **198 per hour** |

**Why the per-client figure is left alone and the other two are divided.** The per-client limiter exists
to bound the work **one caller can cause on a replica**, which is a per-replica quantity by nature; and
the fleet-wide consequence of leaving it at 20 is arithmetic rather than a risk — 120 requests per five
minutes from a single address, each capped at 8 KiB and answered with an empty 204. The other two caps
are fleet-semantic: one bounds the **telemetry volume** the sink of
[06 §9.5](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) retains, the other bounds the **index cardinality** of one
property inside it, and both of those are properties of the workspace, not of a worker. Dividing by the
ceiling is what makes the fleet-wide total obey the number [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)
states.

**And the cost of dividing is stated rather than glossed: at the two-instance floor the effective fleet
ceilings are 666 accepted reports and 66 distinct values per hour**, so the caps bind well before the
fleet figures suggest. That is deliberate — a cap on diagnostic exhaust should fail toward suppressing
early rather than toward an unbounded bill — and it is **visible**, because suppression writes its own
record (below) carrying the budget and the counts, so a reader who sees a thin stream can tell whether it
was quiet or clipped. The divisor is the App Service ceiling because App Service is the primary target;
under the secondary Container Apps option it is that revision's `maxReplicas` and the two budgets are
recomputed from it, which is an arithmetic dependency and not a second design.

**Why the two fleet caps are not backed by the SQL distributed cache the application already has.** It is
the obvious alternative — section [6.3](#63-session-and-cart-identity) already puts a distributed cache
in the application's own database — and each of these four reasons defeats it on its own:

- [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires this endpoint to perform **no read of the
  database** and to write **nothing** to the application database. The cache table is in that database, so
  a shared counter would break the requirement the caps exist to serve.
- It would put a database round trip on a **public, unauthenticated** path — handing an anonymous caller a
  lever on the very resource the endpoint is kept away from.
- `IDistributedCache` offers get, set, refresh and remove and **no atomic increment**, so a shared counter
  is a read-modify-write race. The result would be an approximation *with* a database dependency, where
  the division above is an approximation without one.
- It would place diagnostic exhaust inside the backup and restore position
  [06 §6.7](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) deliberately keeps it out of.

#### 7.5.2 Cardinality overflow collapses to a fixed marker, because a hash preserves the cardinality the cap bounds

An earlier formulation of this contract — and of
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s half of it, which
[§10.2.2.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) has since withdrawn on the same reasoning — replaced a
`blocked-uri` beyond the hourly budget with a **SHA-256 prefix** of itself, recorded under a fixed
`blocked-uri-overflow` marker so that the *count* survived. The intent was right and the mechanism defeated
it: **a digest is injective.**
Distinct attacker-chosen inputs produce distinct prefixes, so retaining one retains exactly the
cardinality the cap was written to bound — 100 000 fabricated values become 100 000 distinct property
values in a 90-day table ([06 §9.5](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)) — and truncating the prefix only
moves the bound to the prefix's own collision space rather than to the budget. What this application
records instead:

| | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Beyond the budget** | The property value is the **fixed literal `blocked-uri-overflow`** — no digest, no prefix, no per-value component of any kind. Every suppressed report carries the identical value, so the property's cardinality beyond the budget is exactly **one** |
| **What is kept** | One **`CspReportSuppressed`** record per replica per hour, carrying the budget, the count of suppressed reports, the count of distinct values dropped and the top `effective-directive` values — a field already reduced to the directive names in [06 §10.2.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s policy, so the summary cannot itself be inflated. It is the summary record [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires, named here so a query can find it; it is **not** a sixth mandatory event in the sense of [06 §9.2.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) and nothing alerts on its absence |
| **What is lost, said plainly** | *Which* URI was blocked beyond that hour's budget. No decision hangs on it: the promotion criteria of [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) resolve a report to a defect or to an approved policy amendment from the **directive** and the values already recorded, and an unbounded tail of attacker-chosen strings informs neither |
| **The second property it buys** | The sink's own memory is bounded too. The distinct-value set never holds more than the budget's entries — 33 strings of at most the 256 characters [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) truncates to — where a digest design needs an unbounded set to know whether it has seen a value before |

**The sink's state, stated because a per-replica hourly budget is mutable shared state reached from a
public path.** One singleton holds a UTC hour stamp, two counters and the bounded set, mutated under a
single lock, with `Interlocked` where a counter is the only thing changing; the window advances by
comparing the stored hour when a report arrives, so there is no timer, no background service and no
registration beyond the singleton. Concurrency is a property of the design rather than an afterthought:
every replica serves reports on many threads at once, and an unsynchronized counter would make the
budget's own numbers wrong in the direction of admitting more.

**What lands in the sink.** `CspViolationReported` at `Warning`, with the field set, the per-field
allow-lists and the truncation rules of [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md), normalized
from both wire shapes into that subsection's one hyphenated record. The *shape* the fields survive in is
section [3.3](#33-the-target-configuration-contract)'s: each is a **named log-state property**, never
interpolated into the message — which is also what that subsection's CWE-117 rule requires, since a value
concatenated into a message text can forge a field boundary in the sink.

**Coverage:** rows **40** and **41** of section [12.4](#124-required-coverage).

## 8. Views, static assets and the wire contracts

### 8.1 Bundling and static assets — no bundler

Five bundles are registered [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:11], [:14], [:19],
[:22], [:26], and two token forms in them are the real obstacle rather than the bundling: a
**`{version}` token** — `"~/Scripts/jquery-{version}.js"` [:12] — and **glob tokens** —
`"~/Scripts/jquery.validate*"` [:15] and `"~/Scripts/modernizr-*"` [:20]. No successor supports either
form ([12 F-12-02](12-migration-blockers.md)).

**Resolution: no bundler at all.**

- The 27 files under `Content/`, `Scripts/`, `Images/` and `fonts/`
  (`git ls-files 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/*' 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Scripts/*' 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Images/*' 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/fonts/*' | wc -l` → `27`) plus the
  web-root `favicon.ico` move to **`wwwroot`**, served by **static-file middleware** (section
  [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order)).
- Cache busting uses the framework's **version-appending tag helper** on `<script>` and `<link>`
  elements, which appends a content hash. That replaces the `{version}` token's purpose — the token
  resolved a *filename* version, the tag helper appends a *content* version, which is strictly better
  for cache correctness and needs no filename convention.
- **The reason a bundler is not reintroduced:** minification and concatenation would require a
  JavaScript toolchain — a package manifest, a lock file, a build step and a CI dependency — for
  **27 asset files** on an application that has no build automation of any kind today
  ([08 §7.2](08-technical-debt-register.md)). That is a permanent build dependency bought for a
  one-time size saving on a catalog application. It is not justified, and if it ever becomes justified
  it is an additive decision taken then.
- **All 11 helper call sites are rewritten**, because both helpers cease to exist along with the five
  bundle virtual paths they name: **10** `@Scripts.Render` and **1** `@Styles.Render`
  (`git grep -o '@Scripts.Render' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' | wc -l` → `10`; the same for
  `@Styles.Render` → `1`). **Four are in the shared layout** — `@Styles.Render("~/Content/css")`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:7], `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/modernizr")`
  [:8], `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/jquery")` [:41] and `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/bootstrap")`
  [:42] — **and the remaining seven** sit in the Account, Checkout and StoreManager views, each inside a
  `@section Scripts` block and each naming the same `~/bundles/jqueryval` path:
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml:35],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:57],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:28],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Register.cshtml:40],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml:8],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Create.cshtml:71] and
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Edit.cshtml:72]. `4 + 7 = 11`. Each becomes a direct
  `<script>` or `<link>` element with the tag helper.
- **Two bundle members do not come across at all**, because the libraries they name are removed rather
  than updated: `respond.js` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:24] and the modernizr
  bundle [:19-20]. Both exist for browsers the target does not support. [04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)
  owns their removal and [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) states the browser matrix; section
  [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) lists the narrowed matrix as an approved delta.
- **The casing is corrected in the move.** The style bundle registers `"~/Content/site.css"`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:28] while the tracked file is
  `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css` — verified: the directory holds `Site.css`,
  `bootstrap.css` and `bootstrap.min.css`, and the registration's lowercase `s` matches none of them.
  IIS resolves this; a case-sensitive filesystem does not, and the stylesheet 404s with no error
  anywhere. Every asset reference is therefore emitted against the **actual** filename after the move.
  [11 §3.7](11-cloud-readiness-assessment.md) owns the finding and
  [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns the audit that gates its hosting recommendation.

Client-side library pins and the acquisition mechanism, including `libman.json`, are
[04 §9](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s. This document names no version.

#### 8.1.1 The per-file disposition of the 27 source assets

**"Relocate the 27 assets" is not a migration plan, and taken literally it produces a broken
application.** Twenty-one of the 27 are the client libraries and their development companions that
[04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) replaces or removes — Bootstrap 3 stylesheets, jQuery
1.10.2, a source map for a file being deleted, two IntelliSense stubs, a vsdoc file, Respond, Modernizr
and the Bootstrap 3 Glyphicon fonts. Copying them into `wwwroot` alongside the pinned successors would
serve two versions of jQuery and two of Bootstrap from one web root. **Only six of the 27 are the
application's own**, and only those relocate.

**How the reference counts below are measured, because the obvious command gets them wrong.** A
repository-wide `git grep` for an asset's file name matches
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/MvcMusicStore.csproj`, whose 61 `<Content Include=…>` items
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/MvcMusicStore.csproj:192-266] name **every** asset by construction — a build
manifest entry is not a reference — and it also matches the two SVG files' own Inkscape export metadata
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Images/logo.svg:18]. Every count in this section is therefore measured over the
surfaces that can actually reference an asset at runtime:

```bash
git grep -n '<pattern>' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' 'src/MVC5/*.cs' \
                           'src/MVC5/*.css'    'src/MVC5/*.config'
```

Every file has exactly one outcome, and the arithmetic closes:

| Source path | Outcome | Target path, or the reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content/Site.css` | **Relocate and adapt** | `wwwroot/css/site.css`. The lowercase target name is deliberate: it settles the mismatch between the registration `"~/Content/site.css"` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:28] and the tracked `Content/Site.css` by standardising on one lowercase convention, and it is where section [8.5.5](#855-contentsitecss--the-named-change-list)'s rule-by-rule rewrite lands |
| `Images/home-showcase.png` | **Relocate** | `wwwroot/images/`. Referenced at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:7] |
| `Images/placeholder.png` | **Relocate** | `wwwroot/images/`. Referenced from the seed constant [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:13], which is why it is also the subject of [06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s data-supplied casing gate |
| `Images/logo.png` | **Relocate — but unreferenced** | `wwwroot/images/`. See the note below |
| `Images/logo.svg` | **Relocate — but unreferenced** | `wwwroot/images/` |
| `Images/placeholder.svg` | **Relocate — but unreferenced** | `wwwroot/images/` |
| `Content/bootstrap.css`, `Content/bootstrap.min.css` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned Bootstrap successor ([04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)) replaces both, and section [8.5](#85-the-bootstrap-upgrade-is-markup-work-not-a-version-bump) is the markup work that makes the replacement safe |
| `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.js`, `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.min.js`, `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.min.map` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned jQuery successor. The `.min.map` is a source map **for a file being deleted**, so it has nothing left to map |
| `Scripts/jquery.validate.js`, `Scripts/jquery.validate.min.js` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned `jquery-validation` successor |
| `Scripts/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.js`, `Scripts/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned `jquery-validation-unobtrusive` successor, which is a **replacement** rather than an update ([04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)) |
| `Scripts/bootstrap.js`, `Scripts/bootstrap.min.js` | **Remove — superseded** | Replaced by the Bootstrap **bundle** file, for the Popper reason [04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) gives |
| `Scripts/_references.js` | **Remove — development-only** | A Visual Studio IntelliSense reference file. It is served to no browser, and the reference probe above for `_references\.js` returns **no match** — nothing in any view, class, stylesheet or configuration file names it |
| `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.intellisense.js` | **Remove — development-only** | An IntelliSense companion, not a runtime file |
| `Scripts/jquery.validate-vsdoc.js` | **Remove — development-only** | A vsdoc companion, not a runtime file |
| `Scripts/respond.js`, `Scripts/respond.min.js` | **Remove — no successor** | A media-query polyfill for Internet Explorer 8. Removal is part of the narrowed browser matrix, an approved delta (section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas)); its bundle membership [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:24] is the rewrite that does not happen (section [8.1.3](#813-the-rendered-tags-and-every-bundle-path-they-replace)) |
| `Scripts/modernizr-2.6.2.js` | **Remove — no successor** | Feature detection for the same era. Its layout call [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:8] is deleted rather than rewritten |
| `fonts/glyphicons-halflings-regular.eot`, `.svg`, `.ttf`, `.woff` | **Remove — unused after the icon decision** | All four exist solely to render the Glyphicons that section [8.5.4](#854-glyphicons-are-removed-rather-than-replaced) removes. No icon library replaces them, so no font files replace them |
| `favicon.ico` (web root, **outside** the 27) | **Relocate** | `wwwroot/`. Worth one note: **no view references it** — the reference probe above for `favicon` returns no match, so there is no `<link rel="icon">` anywhere and the only mention of the file is its build-manifest item [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/MvcMusicStore.csproj:194]. It is served purely by the browser's root-path convention, which the target's static-file middleware satisfies from the same location |

**`1 + 5 + 11 + 3 + 3 + 4 = 27`** — one relocated-and-adapted, five relocated images, eleven superseded,
three development-only, three with no successor, four Glyphicon fonts — plus the favicon, which is
relocated and is not one of the 27.

**Three images are unreferenced, and they are relocated anyway.** `logo.png`, `logo.svg` and
`placeholder.svg` are referenced by nothing: the reference probe above returns **no match** for any of
the three, against exactly one match each for `home-showcase.png`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:7] and `placeholder.png`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:13]. **Deleting brand
assets is a product decision, not a technical-assessment one**, so they move with the rest and are
**flagged for a product decision** rather than dropped on the assessment's own authority. The cost of
carrying them is three files; the cost of being wrong about them is a logo nobody can find.

**The target payload, stated separately from the source inventory, because they are different sets and
different sizes:**

| Group | Count | Contents |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Relocated, application-owned | 7 | `wwwroot/css/site.css`, five files under `wwwroot/images/`, and `wwwroot/favicon.ico` |
| New, application-owned | 1 | `wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js` (section [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script)) |
| Acquired and committed under `wwwroot/lib/` | 5 | Exactly the files [04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s manifest selects — its `files` arrays are explicit and it selects no source maps: `jquery/jquery.min.js`, `jquery-validation/jquery.validate.min.js`, `jquery-validation-unobtrusive/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js`, `bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css` and `bootstrap/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js` |
| **Served total** | **13** | `7 + 1 + 5` |

**Five acquired files from four libraries, and the distinction is the one this row is easiest to get
wrong on.** The manifest has **four** `libraries` entries, but the Bootstrap entry selects **two** files —
the stylesheet and the script bundle — while the three jQuery-family entries select one each, so the file
count is `3 + 2 = 5` rather than 4. [04 §9.3](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) states the three counts
that get conflated here — six source package dispositions, four acquired libraries, five acquired files —
and this row uses the third.

**Two glyphs the target renders are inside one of those files rather than beside them, and that changes a
header rather than this count.** The acquired stylesheet carries its icon-like assets as
`data:image/svg+xml` background images — among them the navbar toggler's glyph consumed by
`.navbar-toggler-icon` and the checked mark of `.form-check-input`, both adopted by section
[8.5.3](#853-non-class-markup-that-changes-with-the-library) and the token matrix of section
[8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens). **No file is added and this table does not
move**: the served total stays **13** and [04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s manifest stays at
five files. What they require is an image content-security-policy that admits the `data:` scheme, which
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns and decides — and the same section requires both
controls to be **seen rendering** under the enforced policy, because a blocked embedded image produces an
empty button and an unticked checkbox with no server-side signal at all.

So the port **serves 13 static files where the source directory holds 28**, and the difference is almost
entirely obsolete vendored libraries and their development companions. Wherever the figure 27 appears in
this document set it is the **assessed source inventory**; the served payload is the table above.

#### 8.1.2 The externalized cart script

**The application has exactly one inline `<script>` block, and it has to leave the page.**
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:7-35] is the whole of the application's
JavaScript — 29 lines inside a `@section Scripts` block [:6], [:36] — and
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires it externalized so the content-security policy
can be `script-src 'self'` with **no `unsafe-inline` and no nonce machinery**. That document owns the
policy; this section owns the artifact, because the target inventory is this document's.

**The artifact:** **`src/MvcMusicStore/wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js`**, mapped from
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:7-35]. It is **page-specific, not
layout-wide** — it binds a handler that exists only on the cart page — so it is emitted from that page's
scripts section rather than from `_Layout.cshtml`, with `asp-append-version="true"` like every other
asset (section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)).

**Its path on disk and its URL are different strings, and only one of them is assertable in a response.**
The file sits at `src/MvcMusicStore/wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js`; the view writes `src="~/js/shopping-cart.js"`;
and the browser receives **`/js/shopping-cart.js`** with a version query string appended. `wwwroot` is the
web root, so it is a prefix the URL never carries — which is why section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) the coverage assertion requires the **public URL** and would fail a correct implementation if
it asserted the disk path.

**Load position and order, which is a correctness requirement and not a preference.** The script calls
`$(function () { … })` [:8] at parse time, so **jQuery must already be loaded when it runs**. The order
is therefore jQuery, then this file, and on the form pages the validation chain must load in its own
fixed order — jQuery, `jquery-validation`, `jquery-validation-unobtrusive` — because each depends on the
previous. [04 §9.3](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) fixes the manifest and the resulting order; this
document renders the tags in it, and section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) asserts on the rendered
order rather than trusting it.

**Required behaviour, itemized against the source so nothing is silently dropped.** Every current
behaviour is preserved; five are added, and each addition is a requirement stated elsewhere rather than
an invention here.

| Behaviour | Source | Target requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind to the removal controls on ready | `$(".RemoveLink").click(…)` [:10] | Unchanged selector — `RemoveLink` is retained as a class hook (section [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens)) — but it now binds to a `<button type="button">` rather than an anchor (section [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **a6**), which is what makes the control keyboard-operable |
| Read the record id and the post URL from the control | `$(this).attr("data-id")`, `$(this).attr("data-url")` [:12-13], guarded by `!= ''` [:14] | Unchanged, guard included. The URL stays server-rendered onto the control rather than constructed in script |
| Post the removal | `$.post(PostToUrl, { "id": recordToDelete }, …)` [:17] | Unchanged **transport**: the body stays **form-urlencoded** with the single field `id`, because that is jQuery's default serialization and no `contentType` is set. **Added:** the `RequestVerificationToken` **header**, read from the page-rendered token — the contract is section [7.4](#74-problem-three--cart-removal-posts-without-a-form)'s and is not restated here |
| Fade out an emptied row | `if (data.ItemCount == 0) { $('#row-' + data.DeleteId).fadeOut('slow') }` [:21-22] | Unchanged, **plus** suppression under `prefers-reduced-motion` (section [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **c5**) and the focus move of item **c4**, because the faded row contains the control that currently holds focus |
| Update a reduced row's count | `$('#item-count-' + data.DeleteId).text(data.ItemCount)` [:24] | Unchanged |
| Update the cart total | `$('#cart-total').text(data.CartTotal)` [:27] | Unchanged |
| Update the message | `$('#update-message').text(data.Message)` [:28] | Unchanged target — the element exists [:44-45] — **plus** the `role="status" aria-live="polite"` attributes on that container (item **c1**), which is what makes the update audible |
| Update the cart badge | `$('#cart-status').text('Cart (' + data.CartCount + ')')` [:29] | **The target element now exists.** Section [8.2.1](#821-the-cartsummary-component-dom-contract) supplies `id="cart-status"` and the same `Cart (n)` format. At a reported count of zero the script removes or hides **`.closest('.nav-item')` from that anchor**, not the anchor itself, so no empty `<li class="nav-item">` is left in the navbar — the contract is 8.2.1's and the traversal is part of it |

**Two properties of the writes, stated because they are easy to lose in a rewrite.**

- **Every DOM write stays text-only.** The source uses `.text(…)` at all four update sites [:24], [:27],
  [:28], [:29] and never `.html(…)`. That is preserved as a **requirement**, not an accident: `Message`
  is composed from the album title [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:75-76],
  and an album title is administrator-supplied free text, so an `.html(…)` rewrite would turn a catalog
  field into a script-injection vector. [09](09-security-assessment.md) owns the exposure; this is the
  line of code that keeps it closed.
- **The payload reads keep their PascalCase names** — **seven reads over five distinct properties**, the
  two extra being on line [:24], which selects by `data.DeleteId` and writes `data.ItemCount` in one
  statement. Section [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy) owns the decision and
  [12 F-12-16](12-migration-blockers.md) states the same five and seven. Moving the code into a file
  changes nothing about either count.

**Three behaviours are added because the source has none of them**, and they are the reason this is a
specified artifact rather than a copy-paste:

- **A pending state.** The control is disabled and carries `aria-busy="true"` from the moment the post
  is issued until it settles, then re-enabled — success **or** failure (item **c2**). Today a
  double-click posts twice.
- **A failure path.** The source handler has a success callback and nothing else [:17-30]: no `.fail`,
  no `error` callback, no status inspection. A rejected removal — including one rejected by the
  anti-forgery validation this port adds — is **completely silent**, and the user believes the item was
  removed. The target handles the failure, leaves the row untouched, and writes a visible message into
  the announced status region (item **c3**).
- **Focus management** across the row removal (item **c4**).

**One consequence for the enforced policy.** With this file in place, the cart page emits **no inline
script at all**, so `script-src 'self'` holds with nothing excepted.
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires cart removal to be exercised under the
**enforced** policy — not merely the report-only phase — before that phase ends, because a blocked
script produces a page that renders perfectly and silently does nothing.

#### 8.1.3 The rendered tags, and every bundle path they replace

[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) fixes the manifest, the file selection and the versions, and
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) fixes the resulting order and the reason for each ordering
constraint. **This document renders them**, and names no version.

**The elements, with their placement.** Every one carries `asp-append-version="true"`, which is what
replaces the `{version}` token's purpose (section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)).

**The `~/` in these attributes is view source, not what the browser sees.** Each element below is written
as it appears in the `.cshtml` file; the tag helper resolves `~/` against the application root and appends
the version, so the rendered `href` and `src` are `/lib/…`, `/css/site.css` and `/js/shopping-cart.js`
with a query string — **never `wwwroot/…`**, which is the web root and appears in no URL. Section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) the coverage assertion requires the rendered form for that reason.

| Where | Element |
| --- | --- |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, in `<head>`, at the position of today's `@Styles.Render` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:7] | `<link rel="stylesheet" href="~/lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css" asp-append-version="true" />` |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, in `<head>`, immediately after it | `<link rel="stylesheet" href="~/css/site.css" asp-append-version="true" />` |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, end of `<body>`, at the position of today's `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/jquery")` [:41] | `<script src="~/lib/jquery/jquery.min.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, immediately after it, at the position of [:42] | `<script src="~/lib/bootstrap/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` |
| Then, unchanged | `@RenderSection("scripts", required: false)` [:43] |
| Each form page's `@section Scripts`, at the position of its `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/jqueryval")` | `<script src="~/lib/jquery-validation/jquery.validate.min.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` then `<script src="~/lib/jquery-validation-unobtrusive/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` |
| The cart page's `@section Scripts` | `<script src="~/js/shopping-cart.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` (section [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script)) |

The seven form-page sites are
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml:35],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:57],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:28],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Register.cshtml:40],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml:8],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Create.cshtml:71] and
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Edit.cshtml:72] — verified with
`git grep -n 'Scripts.Render' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml'`, which returns 10 lines of which these seven name
the validation bundle. **7 + 3 layout script calls = 10 `@Scripts.Render`**, and the layout's single
`@Styles.Render` [:7] completes the 11 of section
[8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler).

**Every one of the five bundle virtual paths, mapped to what replaces it.** Two of the five lose a member
outright, and that is the part a version table hides:

| Bundle | Registered at | Replaced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `~/bundles/jquery` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:11-12] | The one jQuery `<script>` in the layout |
| `~/bundles/jqueryval` | [:14-15] | The **two** validation `<script>` elements, in the fixed order, in each of the seven form pages' scripts sections. One glob token becomes two named files, which is also why the order becomes explicit rather than alphabetical |
| `~/bundles/modernizr` | [:19-20] | **Nothing. There is no replacement element.** The library is removed ([04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)), so the layout's `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/modernizr")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:8] is **deleted**, not rewritten |
| `~/bundles/bootstrap` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:22-24] | The one Bootstrap `<script>` in the layout — **and its second member is dropped**. The bundle includes both `~/Scripts/bootstrap.js` [:23] **and** `~/Scripts/respond.js` [:24]; Respond is removed with no successor, so the bundle's two members become one element |
| `~/Content/css` | [:26-28] | The **two** `<link>` elements in `<head>`, in the order above: the framework stylesheet [:27] then the application's [:28]. The application's own file also **changes path and case** in the move, per section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler) |

**Two bundle members therefore have no target element at all** — `modernizr-*` and `respond.js` — which
is the same fact section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler) states as a consequence of the
browser matrix, expressed here as the two rewrites that do not happen. A port that mechanically rewrote
every `@Scripts.Render` into a `<script>` would emit two elements pointing at files that no longer exist,
and static-file middleware would answer both with 404 while the page rendered normally.

**jQuery is retained only because the unobtrusive validation adapter requires it**, which is
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s statement and is not re-argued here.

### 8.2 Child actions — three view components

Child actions do not exist in the target — [12 F-12-23](12-migration-blockers.md#f-12-23--mvc-child-actions)
is the blocker of record, and this section is its resolution for the migration source. MVC 5 declares
`[ChildActionOnly]` on **three** actions, and **each becomes a view component with its call site**, so
the target contains **three** view components: one class and one `Default.cshtml` per source action, and
no source child action left without a successor. The count matters in both directions — a plan promising
fewer components silently drops a rendered surface, and a plan promising more schedules work with no
source behind it.

| Source action | Renders | Target component | Call site to rewrite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StoreController.GenreMenu` — `[ChildActionOnly]` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs:43], the action body at [:43-55] | The genre navigation in the shared layout | Class **`src/MvcMusicStore/ViewComponents/GenreMenuViewComponent.cs`**, view **`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/GenreMenu/Default.cshtml`** | `@Html.Action("GenreMenu", "Store")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:25] |
| `ShoppingCartController.CartSummary` — `[ChildActionOnly]` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:86], the action body at [:86-99] | The cart count in the same layout | Class **`src/MvcMusicStore/ViewComponents/CartSummaryViewComponent.cs`**, view **`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/CartSummary/Default.cshtml`** | `@Html.Action("CartSummary", "ShoppingCart")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:26] |
| `AccountController.RemoveAccountList` — `[ChildActionOnly]` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:316], the action body at [:316-322] | The external-login removal list on the account-management page | Class **`src/MvcMusicStore/ViewComponents/RemoveAccountListViewComponent.cs`**, view **`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/RemoveAccountList/Default.cshtml`** | `@Html.Action("RemoveAccountList")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22] |

Four specifics:

- **All three components get a typed view model, and the reason is contract safety rather than a missing
  API.** A view component **does** expose `ViewData`, `ViewBag` and `TempData` — `ViewComponent.ViewData`
  returns `ViewComponentContext.ViewData` and `ViewBag` is a dynamic wrapper over it — so the source's
  pattern (`ViewBag.CartCount` and `ViewBag.CartSummary`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:95-96], read by the partial at
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:1], [:4], [:6]) would **compile and
  render** if carried across verbatim. What the target changes is the *direction* data flows: the
  component's `ViewData` is a **defensive copy** of the calling view's, so values the parent set are
  visible inside the component while **values the component sets are not visible to the parent** — the
  one pattern that fails silently. The reason for a typed model is therefore stated correctly:
  `ViewBag.CartCoount` is a runtime nothing in either framework and a compile error against a typed
  model, and a two-property class is a contract two files can be checked against. **Do not justify it
  by claiming view components lack `ViewData` — they do not, and a reviewer who checks that claim will
  discard the recommendation with it.**
- **The two layout components execute in the same request and the same scope, and one reachable case must
  be tested.** A
  child action ran as a nested action invocation; a view component executes inline during the parent's
  render, inside the same request scope and therefore against the **same** scoped `DbContext` as the
  parent's controller (section
  [4.2](#42-what-scoped-registration-actually-changes--and-what-it-does-not)) — including any entities
  that controller has added or modified **without saving**. Two consequences:
  - **No view component ever calls `SaveChangesAsync`.** Stated as a rule, because a component that did
    would commit whatever the parent action had left pending in the tracker.
  - **One target request genuinely reaches that state, and it is the test to write.** Of the three
    actions that write, `AddToCart` and a successful checkout both **redirect** — so the page that
    renders the components is a *different* request with a *different* scope and proves nothing — and
    `RemoveFromCart` returns JSON, which renders no layout and therefore no components at all. The one
    that does not is the **checkout failure path**: it returns `View(input)` after the write attempt
    (section [8.10](#812-the-checkout-write-path--one-ordered-contract)), so the layout — and with it
    both layout components — renders in a request whose context still tracks the added-but-uncommitted
    order and order-detail entities. The coverage assertion requires that both layout components render
    correctly there **and that nothing is persisted by that render**, which is the assertion the
    redirect-crossing test it replaces could never have made.
- **`RemoveAccountListViewComponent` is the third, and its model is where the adaptation work sits.** The
  source action reads the signed-in user's linked logins and passes them to a partial whose model is
  `ICollection<Microsoft.AspNet.Identity.UserLoginInfo>`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:1], with the remove button gated on
  `ViewBag.ShowRemoveButton` [:13] set from `HasPassword() || linkedAccounts.Count > 1`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:319-321]. Three things change and nothing
  else:
  - **The type name survives, the namespace and the producing API do not.** `UserLoginInfo` keeps its
    name under `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity`, but its shape differs — it carries
    `ProviderDisplayName` in addition to `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` — and it is obtained from
    `UserManager.GetLoginsAsync(user)` returning `IList<UserLoginInfo>` rather than from
    `UserManager.GetLogins(userId)`. So this is a namespace update **plus** an adaptation of how the
    collection is obtained and what the view reads from each element, not a rename.
  - **`ViewBag.ShowRemoveButton` becomes a model property**, for the reason the first specific gives: a
    value the *component* sets is not visible to the parent, and a value the parent sets is not the one
    the component computes. The component's model carries `IReadOnlyList<UserLoginInfo> Logins` and
    `bool ShowRemoveButton`, computed inside `InvokeAsync` from the same two conditions as the source.
  - **The removal form's contract is preserved exactly.** The `Default.cshtml` posts `loginProvider` and
    `providerKey` to `Disassociate`
    [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:19-20], which is the action kept
    authorized in section [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths);
    the anti-forgery token [:17] is emitted by the form tag helper instead of the explicit call, and
    validated by the global filter of section [7.1](#71-the-policy).

  The `@Html.Action` call at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22] becomes a component
  invocation and the `<section id="externalLogins">` block that contains it [:21-24] is **kept**.

  **The one behavioural difference this conversion introduces, stated precisely because the loose version
  overstates it.** `/Account/RemoveAccountList` is not usable today either: the conventional route matches
  it, and `[ChildActionOnly]`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:316] then rejects the direct request by
  throwing, which the global `HandleErrorAttribute`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:10] turns into an error page. In the target **no route
  matches at all**, because a view component is not addressable, so the same request answers **404**
  instead. The capability is unchanged and the status code is not — which is why it is recorded as
  approved delta 11 rather than as a preserved contract, and asserted by the coverage assertion.
- **The two layout components query the database on every page render today, and the target treats them
  differently from each other — one is cached, one is scoped, and neither goes in the distributed cache.**
  This is the fourth specific and the only one that is a performance decision rather than a portability
  one. [11 §3.8.2](11-cloud-readiness-assessment.md) records the uncached per-request aggregate as a
  readiness finding and names **[06 §6.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)** as the owner of cache
  **placement and sizing**. That section's decision is that **the session cache table is sized for session
  only and the per-request aggregate is cached in memory per instance rather than in the SQL cache**, on
  the ground that the aggregate is identical for all users, tolerates staleness measured in minutes, and is
  cheap to recompute on a cold instance — so routing it through a database round trip to avoid a database
  round trip would be self-defeating. This document owns the mechanism that implements that placement, and
  it is three decisions.

  **There is one policy, not two, and the register that supplies the evidence says so explicitly.**
  [08 §5.2](08-technical-debt-register.md) is the source of the fact that changes the shape of this
  mechanism — that **four** distinct writes move the aggregate's ranking key, not one: a checkout, an album
  **create**, an album **delete**, and an album **edit that reassigns `GenreId`**, which moves an album's
  entire accumulated quantity between genres **with no order written at all**. That register states the
  remediation as "one policy governs this and it is not set here" and names this section as the owner of
  the mechanism, [06 §6.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) as the owner of placement and sizing, and
  the requirement that a policy **account for all four triggers** rather than silently answer three. The
  table below is that accounting, and the staleness it tolerates is stated **once**, in its second row: the
  three administration writes evict, the order write does not, and the resulting bounded lag is a named
  decision rather than an omission. No second staleness statement appears anywhere in this document.

  | Component | Target treatment |
  | --- | --- |
  | **`GenreMenuViewComponent`** — the nested `Sum` over each genre's albums' order-detail quantities, ordered and taken nine at a time [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs:46-52] | **Cached per instance in `IMemoryCache`**, never in the distributed cache. One entry under a single fixed key; the cached value is the **component's own view model** — the nine genres in ranked order, projected to the fields the view reads — and never tracked entities, so no `DbContext`-attached object outlives its request scope inside a process-wide cache. **`GenreMenuCacheTtl`, five minutes** by default and configuration with that default, expressed as an **absolute** expiration and not a sliding one: a sliding window on a key touched by every page render never expires, which would turn "staleness measured in minutes" into staleness measured in the deployment's lifetime. **Stampede control is required rather than optional**: a cold instance under load must compute the aggregate **once**, so the entry is populated under a per-key `SemaphoreSlim` and concurrent renders await that computation — otherwise the first seconds after every scale-out event run one nested aggregate per in-flight request, which is precisely the load this cache exists to remove |
  | **Explicit invalidation, which the TTL does not replace — three of [08 §5.2](08-technical-debt-register.md)'s four triggers** | The three administration writes — **create**, **edit** and **delete** in `StoreManagerController` — **evict the key after a successful `SaveChangesAsync`**, in the same request, so an administrator who adds or removes an album sees the menu reflect it on the next page rather than up to five minutes later. **The edit case evicts unconditionally rather than only when `GenreId` changed**: that register's reassignment trigger is the subtle one, an edit is rare, and a conditional eviction would depend on comparing the loaded and posted keys correctly on a path whose failure is invisible. Eviction is **after** the save and never before, so the rule "the cache follows the committed state" holds without a second case. **The fourth trigger, the order write, deliberately does *not* evict** — the one staleness statement in this document, made here: a checkout adds `OrderDetails.Quantity` and so can reorder the menu, but evicting on every order would make the cache useless on exactly the traffic it exists for, and a nine-entry popularity ranking that lags by at most `GenreMenuCacheTtl` is the staleness [06 §6.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) states is tolerated. **So all four triggers are accounted for and none is silently unanswered**: three by eviction, one by a bounded window with a named bound |
  | **`CartSummaryViewComponent`** — the badge | **Not cached at all, and scoped instead.** It is per-user, it changes on every add and removal, and a cache keyed per cart would be a per-user entry invalidated by the same writes it is meant to spare — cost without benefit. What changes is the **query**: the source materializes the cart's rows and reads `a.Album.Title` per row [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:91-93], which is lazy-loading site a4 of section [4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy) and one round trip per line under EF Core's explicit-loading rules; the target issues **one projection query** filtered on the cart key selecting `Album.Title` only, materializing no `Cart` and no `Album` entity. **The badge's semantics are preserved exactly by that projection**, per the two-cart-counts rule of section [4.8](#48-the-service-layer-and-the-two-patterns-deliberately-not-adopted): the count is a **count of lines** and not a sum of quantities, `Distinct()` applies to the tooltip text only and never to the count, the titles are ordered by title, and a zero count renders **no badge element** rather than a badge reading `0` |

  **The distributed cache stays session-only, and that is the boundary this bullet exists to hold.** The
  SQL-backed cache of section [6.3](#63-session-and-cart-identity) carries session and nothing else; the
  genre aggregate is never written to it, because that cache is backed by the very database it would be
  sparing. If a distributed home for the aggregate is ever wanted — a fleet large enough that per-instance
  cold starts matter — 06 §6.4 states that it is a separate decision with its own sizing and that a
  **dedicated cache service**, not the session cache table, would be its home. **The coverage assertion
  asserts the TTL bound, the eviction on an administration write, the non-eviction on an order, the
  single-computation property under concurrency, and the scoped badge query's round-trip count.

#### 8.2.1 The `CartSummary` component DOM contract

**Why this component alone gets a specified DOM contract.** It is the only rendered surface in the
application that **two** code paths write: the server renders it into every page from the shared layout
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:26], and the cart page's script rewrites it after a
removal [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:29]. **Today those two paths do not
agree on anything** — not the element, not the format and not even the quantity — and the disagreement is
invisible only because the script's write lands nowhere. Three separate defects, established before the
target is stated:

| Defect | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| **The script's target element does not exist.** `$('#cart-status').text(…)` addresses an id **no view in the application emits**, so the header badge never updates after a removal | `git grep -n cart-status -- src/MVC5` returns exactly one line, the write itself [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:29]. The component renders an unadorned `<li>` and `<a>` with no `id` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:3-4] |
| **The two paths compute different quantities under the same name.** The component renders the number of **cart line rows**; the removal response's `CartCount` is the **sum of quantities** | Component: `ViewBag.CartCount = cartItems.Count()` over `GetCartItems().Select(a => a.Album.Title)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:91-95]. Response: `CartCount = cart.GetCount()` [:78], which sums `cartItems.Count` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:103-112]. **One album with five copies renders as `1` and would be written back as `5`** |
| **Removing the Glyphicon leaves an unlabelled digit.** The rendered content is a pictogram plus a bare number, and approved delta 6 removes the pictogram | `<span class="glyphicon glyphicon glyphicon-shopping-cart"></span>` — note the token is **duplicated** in the source — followed by `@ViewBag.CartCount` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:5-6] |

**The target contract, stated once and consumed by section
[8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script) and section [12.4](#124-required-coverage):**

- **Element and structure.** The component renders `<li class="nav-item">` containing
  `<a class="nav-link" href="…ShoppingCart/Index">`, because it renders into the navbar list
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:23], [:26] and section
  [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens) requires those two classes on a navbar
  item and link.
- **The stable identifier is `id="cart-status"`, on the anchor.** That is **the id the existing script
  already expects** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:29], so the contract is
  satisfied by making the server emit what the client was always written against, rather than by
  changing the client. The `id` — not a class and not a data attribute — is the authoritative selector,
  and the externalized script selects on it; `RemoveLink` stays a class because it identifies **many**
  controls, one per row, while this identifies exactly one element.
- **Content is a visible textual label and the count together, rendered as `Cart (n)`.** That is exactly
  the string the script writes [:29], so after the port the server-rendered and script-updated states
  are **the same string produced two ways** — which is the property that makes the disagreement above
  impossible rather than merely unlikely.
- **`n` is the total quantity**, the definition the response's `CartCount` already carries
  ([8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy) preserves that property's name and
  meaning), so **the component is aligned to `GetCount()`**. Two alternatives were considered and
  rejected: adding a line-count property to the response widens a wire contract this port deliberately
  keeps byte-identical, and leaving the two definitions disagreeing would convert today's invisible
  inconsistency into a visible one the moment the script's target exists.
- **Zero-count behaviour, on both paths, and what "the element" means is stated exactly.** The
  server-rendered path already gets this right and is preserved: `@if (ViewBag.CartCount > 0)`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:1] wraps the **entire `<li>`** [:3-8], so
  at zero count the component renders **nothing at all** — no empty badge and **no empty list item**.
  **The script must match that, which means it operates on the list item and not on the anchor.** The
  stable identifier `cart-status` is on the *anchor*, so a script that removed or hid only the element it
  selected would leave `<li class="nav-item">` behind — empty, still occupying its box in the navbar, and
  still announced as a list item by a screen reader. The requirement is therefore explicit: on a response
  reporting a count of zero the script resolves **`.closest('.nav-item')` from the identified anchor** and
  removes or hides **that** ancestor, so the two paths produce the same DOM at the boundary rather than
  two DOMs that merely look alike. The traversal is named rather than left as "the element" because that
  phrasing is exactly what produces the surviving empty parent. The script never has to *create* the
  element: a removal cannot increase the count, so if the anchor is absent the count was already zero and
  no update is due.
- **`ViewBag.CartCount` and `ViewBag.CartSummary`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:95-96] become typed view-model
  properties**, for the reason section [8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components) gives for all
  three components.
- **The `title` attribute is preserved, with its limitation recorded rather than quietly fixed.** It
  carries the **newline-joined** list of distinct album titles —
  `string.Join("\n", cartItems.Distinct())`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:96], rendered at
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:4] — and it is carried across unchanged.
  **The response carries no summary field**, so the tooltip is **not refreshed** after a removal; it
  becomes accurate again on the next page render. That staleness exists today and the port preserves it.
  Adding a summary field to the response is **out of scope**: it is a wire-contract change for a tooltip,
  and section [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy)'s whole argument is that
  this endpoint's payload stays as it is.
- **The count change is announced**, through the live region of section
  [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **c1** — a silently mutating number in
  the page header is exactly the update a screen-reader user would otherwise never learn about.

**This is approved delta 11** (section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas)), owner **Product**,
and its two visible consequences are named there rather than discovered at review: the pictogram gives
way to the word `Cart`, and the number changes meaning from line count to total quantity — visible only
for a cart holding more than one copy of some album. The rendered comparison is on section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual)'s checklist.

### 8.3 The five views that name legacy types

**A plan that treats all 29 views as a bulk copy breaks in exactly these five places.**
(`git ls-files 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' | wc -l` → `29`.) Each is listed with its line-level problem and its
resolution.

**(1) `Views/Shared/Error.cshtml` — a removed model type, and the application's first real error
policy.**

`@model System.Web.Mvc.HandleErrorInfo` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Error.cshtml:1]. The type
does not exist in the target and the exception-handling middleware supplies **no Razor equivalent**, so
there is nothing to substitute into the directive. The rest of the file is two static headings [:7-8]
and it renders **no property of the model at all**.

**Resolution: define `ErrorViewModel.cs` and specify the whole policy, because the source has none to
preserve.** `HandleErrorAttribute` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:10] engages when custom errors
are in effect, and **no edition declares `<customErrors>`** — there is no live element in any
configuration file in the repository (verified; command in
[Appendix A](#appendix-a--reproducibility); [09 §6.10](09-security-assessment.md) owns the finding).

**That absence does not make the attribute inert, and the plausible reading of it is wrong.** With
`<customErrors>` undeclared, classic ASP.NET applies its default of **`RemoteOnly`**, which means custom
errors are *on* for every non-local client and off only for a browser on the server itself. So as
shipped the filter does engage for a remote visitor: it returns the shared `Error.cshtml` with a
**500**, while a developer browsing from the machine hosting the site sees the framework's own
exception page instead. The behaviour is therefore not absent but **split by caller location, and
stated nowhere** — which is exactly why [09 §6.10](09-security-assessment.md) records it as a framework
default nobody chose.

**The target's error behaviour is consequently being chosen, not preserved** — not because nothing
happens today, but because what happens today depends on where the client is and is not a policy anyone
wrote down. Two things follow for the delta table in section
[11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas): the **uniformity** of the target's behaviour is the
change (one generic response for every caller, local or remote), and the status code for an unhandled
exception is **preserved** at 500 rather than altered. It is therefore stated in full:

**The action that produces the model.** One action serves both paths, because both render the same
view and differ only in the status they carry:

```csharp
// Controllers/HomeController.cs
[AllowAnonymous]
[ResponseCache(NoStore = true, Location = ResponseCacheLocation.None)]
public IActionResult Error(int? id)
{
    // The route segment is public input. Only a real error status may be echoed back
    // as the response status; anything else — including a success code, a negative
    // number and a value no HTTP status can be — is normalised to 500.
    var statusCode = id is int code && code >= 400 && code <= 599
        ? code
        : StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError;

    Response.StatusCode = statusCode;
    return View(new ErrorViewModel
    {
        StatusCode = statusCode,
        TraceIdentifier = Activity.Current?.Id ?? HttpContext.TraceIdentifier
    });
}
```

**Why the range test is not defensive decoration.** `/Home/Error/{id}` is a route on the public URL
surface — it has to be, because `UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute` and `AccessDeniedPath` both reach the
action through it — so **any client can choose the value**. Writing it to `Response.StatusCode`
unfiltered has three distinct consequences, and the first is a contradiction of this section's own
contract:

- **`/Home/Error/200` would answer `200 OK` with an error page in it** — precisely the defect the
  "neither error path ever returns 200" rule below exists to close, reachable by typing a URL. The same
  goes for `/Home/Error/302` and any other non-error code.
- **A negative or oversized value is not a status code at all.** `Response.StatusCode` accepts a bounded
  range, so `/Home/Error/-1` or `/Home/Error/99999` throws inside the response pipeline — an unhandled
  exception raised *by the error handler*, on an anonymous route, which is both a 500 whose cause is the
  error path itself and a trivially repeatable log-noise generator.
- **A non-numeric segment** — `/Home/Error/abc` — fails to bind, leaves `id` null, and normalises to 500
  with no error of its own. That is already the desired behaviour and the test asserts it.

**The clamp cannot alter a genuine error response**, which is what makes it free.
`UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute` re-executes only for responses already in the 400-599 range, and the
three codes this application produces through it — 404, 405 and 403 via `AccessDeniedPath` — are all
inside it, as is the 500 the exception handler sets. So every value the framework supplies passes the
test unchanged, and only a client-chosen value is replaced. The coverage assertion requires both directions.

Four further details in that signature are contractual rather than stylistic:

- **The parameter is named `id`, deliberately.** `UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/Home/Error/{0}")`
  (section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order)) substitutes the status code into the path, so
  the request re-executes as `/Home/Error/404` — and under the single conventional route
  `{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}` that third segment binds to a parameter called **`id`**.
  Naming it `code` would leave it null on every request and every status-code response would render as
  500. `AccessDeniedPath = "/Home/Error/403"` (section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled))
  binds through the same segment, which is why that path needs no route of its own.
- **`[AllowAnonymous]` is explicit.** `HomeController` carries no `[Authorize]` today, so the attribute
  is not strictly required — but the access-denied and 401 paths route *here*, and an error page that
  can itself be refused produces a redirect loop. Stating it means a later `[Authorize]` on the
  controller cannot create one.
- **The action sets the response status itself.** On the re-executed path the middleware has already
  preserved the original code, so the assignment writes the same value and is a no-op. On the
  access-denied **redirect** — which is a fresh 200-status request, not a re-execution — the assignment
  is the only thing that makes the response a **403** rather than a 200 with an error page in it.
- **No caching.** An error response cached by a proxy or the browser outlives the condition that caused
  it.

**What populates `ErrorViewModel`, exhaustively.** Two properties, both safe in every environment:

| Property | Value | Rendered? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StatusCode` | `id` when the route supplied a value **in 400-599**, otherwise `500` — the clamp above | Not rendered as a number in the view; it is available so a later refinement can vary the heading by code without changing the contract |
| `TraceIdentifier` | `Activity.Current?.Id ?? HttpContext.TraceIdentifier` — the distributed-trace id when one exists, the request id otherwise | **Yes**, so a user can quote a value that correlates to the log record |

**The error view renders without the shared layout, and this is a correctness requirement rather than a
styling choice.** `Views/Shared/Error.cshtml` declares no `Layout`, so `_ViewStart.cshtml` supplies
`~/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/_ViewStart.cshtml:2] — and in the target
that layout hosts the two **layout** view components of section
[8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components) — the third renders only on the account-management page —
**both of which query the catalog
database on every render**: the genre navigation runs the nested aggregate and the cart summary reads the
cart. Inherit the layout and the error page becomes a page that cannot render when the database is
unavailable, which is one of the conditions most likely to have produced the error in the first place.
The failure that follows is worse than the original: an exception thrown *while* the exception handler is
re-executing the error path cannot be handled by that same handler, so the client receives a bare 500
with no body, or a reset connection, and the log records a rendering failure whose cause is the error
page rather than the fault.

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Layout** | `@{ Layout = null; }` declared **in the error view itself**, so no `_ViewStart` can reintroduce one, or a dedicated `_ErrorLayout.cshtml` containing only static markup — **no view component, no tag helper that queries, no partial that reads the database, and no injected service** |
| **What the page may contain** | The two static headings, preserved verbatim [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Error.cshtml:7-8], the trace identifier, and static assets. It may render before any database call succeeds |
| **Navigation** | A plain link to `/`, not the layout's genre menu — the menu is exactly the component that cannot run |
| **The same rule for status-code pages** | `/Home/Error/{code}` renders the same layout-free view, because a 404 is served under the same conditions and by the same action |

**The persistence-failure classifier — one classifier, owned here, consumed by every handler whose
failure response is a redisplay.** Any write path that answers a failure by redisplaying its own view
