| d2 | **No rule removes the framework focus ring for keyboard focus, and the single pointer-only exception is named.** Stated as a prohibition because it is the most common way a port loses keyboard visibility, and the application stylesheet is small enough to verify by reading. **The one permitted rule is `a:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: 0 }`** — group 2 of section [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses), owned as **approved delta 19** — which suppresses the ring for a pointer click only and leaves keyboard focus indicated. A rule that removes the ring for `:focus-visible`, or one that removes it unconditionally, fails this item | 86 lines [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:1-86], none of which does this today. The **library** does, on two selectors — `.dropdown-toggle:focus { outline: 0 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:3231-3233] and `.open > a { outline: 0 }` [:3313-3315] — which is why the prohibition is written against the port's own stylesheet rather than against "the source" as a whole |
| d3 | **Three colour pairs are measured with a contrast tool at implementation time, against a stated numeric threshold, and the measured ratios are recorded in the review artifact.** The pairs: **(i)** `#ddd` navbar text and brand on the navbar background [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:72-82], the background being the `#222222` preserved by section [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses); **(ii)** `#b94a48` validation text on the page background [:20-22], [:36-38]; **(iii)** the button label against its fill, which is new to this list because **approved delta 16** changes that fill from white-with-dark-text to a solid secondary — the one pair whose value the port itself moves. **The thresholds are the pass criteria: 4.5:1 for normal-size text, and 3:1 for large-scale text — 24px, or 18.66px when bold — and for the visual boundaries of user-interface components.** All three pairs above are normal-size text at their rendered sizes, including the 18px navbar brand [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4194-4199], so all three are measured against **4.5:1**; the button's own border against the page background is measured against **3:1** as a component boundary. **A threshold on named pairs is an objective acceptance check and is not a conformance claim** — this section still asserts nothing about any standard as a whole (see the scope note above), and the artifact records ratios, not a verdict on the application | as cited |
| d4 | **One further pair is measured and reported without blocking**: the `#cccccc` input border [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1719-1733] against the white page background, a component boundary whose threshold is 3:1. It is separated from d3 because it is **preserved source appearance** — section [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) pins that border deliberately — so a failure here is an **inherited** defect the measurement surfaces, recorded with a named owner and a proposed replacement value, and it does **not** fail the port. This distinction exists so the review can separate a contrast defect the port *introduced* from one it faithfully preserved, and so neither gets hidden by the other | as cited |

**Acceptance is split by what kind of fact each item is**, because half of this list is checkable by a
machine and half is not, and conflating the two is how an accessibility requirement ends up unverified.

| Kind of fact | Items | Where it is established |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Attributes and structure in the rendered response** | **a1**, **a3**, **a4**, **a5**, **a5b**, **a6**, **b2**, **b3**, **c1** | Section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 28, as response-level assertions that re-run on every change — with **a5b** asserted on the rendered Registered Logins state of row 32, since the table exists only when the account has a linked login |
| **Attributes on a *conditional* render** | **a2** (the dropdown's `role` and menu-item classes), **b4** (`aria-invalid` on a failed field), **b5** (the validation summary) | Section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) — a2 within row 9, **b5 within row 30** and **b4 within row 31**, since each needs a specific page state to be rendered at all |
| **Already covered by an owned decision** | **a7** (the sign-out control, delta 13), **b1** (label association through the typed helpers) | Row 20 and the form rows of section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) |
| **Runtime behaviour** | **c2**, **c3**, **c4**, **c5** | The **interaction-state pass** of the manual review, [07 §7.3](07-effort-risks-sequencing.md). A response-level suite cannot observe a disabled state, an announcement, a focus move or a suppressed animation |
| **Rendered appearance and measurement** | **d1**, **d2**, **d3**, **d4** | The same manual review. **d3**'s three ratios and **d4**'s one are recorded **as measured values against their stated thresholds** — 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for component boundaries — so a failure is a defect with a named owner rather than a silent pass, and d4's failure is reported as inherited rather than as a port regression |

**No row of that table asserts conformance to a standard**, and
[07 §7.3](07-effort-risks-sequencing.md) is explicit that its artifact records **requirements met**, not
conformance.

### 8.10 Absent album art — the rendering rule

**This section exists because the write path keeps a field optional and the read path has never defined
what an empty one looks like.** `Album.AlbumArtUrl` carries `[DisplayName("Album Art URL")]` and
`[StringLength(1024)]` and **no `[Required]`** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Album.cs:26-28], and
[06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) preserves that optionality explicitly rather than letting
a security validator turn it into a mandatory field. Preserving the write side raises the read side as a
question this document owns: **three views render the value, and today they do not agree with each other
about an album that has none.**

| Render site | What the source does with an absent value |
| --- | --- |
| `<img alt="@album.Title" src="@Url.Content( @album.AlbumArtUrl)" />` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:15] | **Unguarded.** An `<img>` element is emitted whatever the value is, with its `src` being whatever `Url.Content` returns for a null, empty or whitespace-only path — which cannot be a resolvable image path, so the element resolves to no image |
| `@if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(album.AlbumArtUrl)) { <img … /> }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:15-18] | **Guarded, and the guard omits the element entirely** — the anchor renders with the title heading [:19] and no image at all. The guard is `String.IsNullOrEmpty`, so a **whitespace-only** value takes the unguarded branch and behaves like the two sites above |
| `<img alt="@Model.Title" src="@Url.Content(@Model.AlbumArtUrl)" />` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Details.cshtml:10] | **Unguarded**, exactly as the home page is |

So the source has **no defined absent-image presentation**: one site omits the image, two emit an image
element that cannot resolve, and the guard that exists misses one of the three forms of absence. That is
a gap rather than a contract, which is why the target states a rule instead of preserving a behaviour.

**The target rule, applied identically at all three sites.** The condition is
`String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(album.AlbumArtUrl)` — the same test
[06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s validator applies, so the write side and the read side
classify absence the same way and a value the validator accepted as absent renders as absent. When the
condition holds, the view renders the placeholder asset already in the served inventory —
`wwwroot/images/placeholder.png`, relocated by section
[8.1.1](#811-the-per-file-disposition-of-the-27-source-assets) — and keeps the album title as its `alt`,
so the image alternative stays meaningful and requirement **a3** of section
[8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) is not undermined by a second unlabelled
image. When the condition does not hold, the stored value is rendered exactly as it is today. **No new
artifact is added**: the placeholder is one of the five images section 8.1.1 already relocates, so the
served total of 13 files is unchanged.

**It is an approved delta, not a silent improvement**, and it is delta **17** of section
[11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas). Two of the three sites change what they render for an album
with no image path — from an image element that resolves to nothing into a placeholder image — and the
third changes from rendering nothing into rendering the placeholder. Every one of those is visible on the
page, which is precisely the class of change that needs an owner rather than an implementer's judgement.
**Product** owns it, and the alternative the owner can choose instead is stated so the decision is real:
omit the element at all three sites, matching the catalog view's current guard, which preserves one of
the three source behaviours and leaves a ragged grid where an album has no art.

**How much of the committed data this touches: none.** [03](03-modernization-roadmap.md) W5's measured
baseline is **one distinct value** across the catalog and it is the local placeholder path, so no album in
the committed database renders through this rule on day one. It governs future administrator input and
any non-committed source database the migration is pointed at — the same scope
[06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) gives its `http://` branch, and for the same reason.

Coverage is section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 33, which asserts the blank-save-then-render path
end to end rather than only the validator.

---

## 9. A namespace substitution table is not a transformation plan

This section exists because writing a `FROM → TO` import table and calling it a migration plan is the
single most likely structural error in this port, and it is a tempting one: nineteen of twenty-seven
source files carry a legacy `using` directive, so a table looks like it covers the work. **It does not.
The imports are a symptom; the file's role in the target is the plan.**

### 9.1 The census, and how to count it

**19 of the 27 `.cs` files** in the migration source carry at least one directive naming a namespace
that does not survive the port.

**A methodology note that changes the answer.** All 27 files carry a **UTF-8 byte-order mark**, so a
naive `^\s*using` match against the file decoded as UTF-8 sees the BOM as a leading character on line 1
and **misses a first-line directive**. That count returns **17**. A BOM-tolerant per-file census
returns **19**. Both commands and both results are in
[Appendix A](#appendix-a--reproducibility) so the difference is checkable rather than asserted.

**One row below states a different number from the frozen plan, and the BOM does not explain that
one**: `using System.Web;` is **11** files measured here and **10** in the plan's own census. **That is
not an open question. The plan's own §0.11.3 supplies the governing rule — "Where a deliverable and the
repository disagree, the repository wins" — so 11 is the authoritative figure**, and the table below and
every use of the count in this document state it. It is reproducible by a
BOM-insensitive command — `git grep -n 'using System.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -v 'System\.Web\.'`
returns **11** lines, one per file — whose full output is printed beside the record in section
[9.3](#93-two-plan-correction-records-for-the-plan-owner). The BOM-sensitive form returns **9**, so it
accounts for neither figure; what accounts for the plan's 10 is a **single file omitted from its list**,
and section [9.3](#93-two-plan-correction-records-for-the-plan-owner) item 1 names it with both
commands' output. That record is a **plan-correction record notifying the plan owner** rather than a
question awaiting an answer.

Per-directive counts, BOM-tolerant, counted as **files containing the directive**:

| Directive | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `using System.Web.Mvc;` | 11 |
| `using System.Web;` | 11 |
| `using Microsoft.Owin*` | 4 |
| `using Microsoft.AspNet.Identity*` | 4 |
| `using System.Data.Entity;` | 3 |
| `using Owin;` | 3 |
| `using System.Web.Routing;` | 2 |
| `using System.Web.Optimization;` | 2 |
| `using System.Configuration;` | 1 |

Two observations from that table rather than from the total. **`using System.Web.Mvc;` reaches the
model layer** — [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Order.cs:4] and
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:5] — so the port is not confined to `Controllers/`. And
**`using System.Configuration;`** appears exactly once, at
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:7], which is the file whose reads at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:23-24] are the
reason the options pattern is required (section
[3.1](#31-configuration-webconfig-becomes-appsettingsjson-read-through-iconfiguration)).

### 9.2 The four groups

Every file's disposition is set by its **role**, not by its imports, and the 27 files fall into four
groups that need four different kinds of work. The four groups are a **partition**: each of the 27
paths appears in exactly one group, each group's stated count equals the number of paths listed under
it, and `8 + 6 + 5 + 8 = 27`. The command that produces the 27 paths is in
[Appendix A](#appendix-a--reproducibility), so the partition is checkable against the checkout rather
than taken on trust.

**Group A — eight files that are deleted, so no import in them is ever rewritten.** Their `Owin`,
`Microsoft.Owin.*`, `System.Web`, `System.Web.Mvc`, `System.Web.Routing`, `System.Web.Optimization`
and `System.Configuration` directives **simply cease to exist**. A substitution table applied to this
group produces eight rewritten files that should not exist.

| File | Where its responsibility goes |
| --- | --- |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Global.asax.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Global.asax.cs:11-21] | Split across `Program.cs` and middleware, registration by registration — section [2.2](#22-the-five-application_start-registrations-do-not-share-one-fate) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Startup.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Startup.cs:4-14] | `Program.cs`; `IAppBuilder` has no successor type — section [2.3](#23-owin-startup-the-abstraction-goes-the-responsibilities-do-not) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/RouteConfig.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/RouteConfig.cs:16-20] | The endpoint registration in `Program.cs` — section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:10] | Exception-handling middleware plus the global anti-forgery filter — sections [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) and [7.1](#71-the-policy) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:14-45] | Its provisioning half becomes `tools/provision-admin` (section [10](#10-administrator-provisioning-becomes-an-operator-command)); its initializer call becomes migrations (section [5](#5-schema-lifecycle-and-the-two-data-migrations)) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:11-20] | `AddAuthentication().AddCookie()` in `Program.cs`, under the explicit policy of section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:11-28] | **Nowhere — the responsibility ends.** There is no bundler in the target (section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:8-13] | **Absorbed by MSBuild properties** in the SDK-style project — [04 §5.3](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) |

Seven of the eight carry at least one legacy directive; `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` carries none and
is in this group because it is deleted, not because of what it imports.

**Group B — six files whose disposition is a change of identity: the file becomes a different file,
becomes two files, or sheds a responsibility into a file that does not exist yet.** The substitution
rules below do occur inside these six, but they are a detail of a larger rewrite rather than the work
itself.

- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs` is not import-rewritten — it is
  rewritten wholesale**, `using Microsoft.Owin.Security;`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:10] included, because `ChallengeResult`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:394] and its `ExecuteResult` override
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:411] have no direct target and because its
  entire Identity surface changes shape. Section
  [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) records the decision that removes the
  provider-driven half of it outright and ports the linked-login half as a view component. This is the
  file [08 §4.2](08-technical-debt-register.md) sizes at 382 non-blank lines — roughly 18 percent of
  the migration source by the sizing metric — and the one part of the port with no line-for-line
  successor.
- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs` stops being a model.** It loses its `System.Web`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:4] and `System.Web.Mvc`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:5] directives, loses the dead `Controller` overload
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:29-32], and becomes
  `Services/ShoppingCartService.cs` (section
  [4.8](#48-the-service-layer-and-the-two-patterns-deliberately-not-adopted)). Its file path, its
  namespace, its registration and its consumers all change.
- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/IdentityModels.cs` becomes two files.** It declares two unrelated
  types in one file: `ApplicationUser : IdentityUser`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/IdentityModels.cs:6-8], which becomes `Models/ApplicationUser.cs`,
  and `ApplicationDbContext : IdentityDbContext<ApplicationUser>`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/IdentityModels.cs:10-16], which becomes
  `Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs` and trades the `base("DefaultConnection")` convention
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/IdentityModels.cs:13] for an explicit `DbContextOptions` constructor
  (section [4.5](#45-two-contexts-two-migration-sets-two-history-tables)). The split is not cosmetic:
  the two land in different folders with different responsibilities, and the context is the one that
  acquires the `IDataProtectionKeyContext` implementation of section
  [5.3](#53-who-applies-ddl-and-in-what-order).
- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/MusicStoreEntities.cs` moves and gains a constructor.** It becomes
  `Data/MusicStoreEntities.cs`, keeps its six `DbSet` properties
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/MusicStoreEntities.cs:7-12], and **gains an explicit
  `DbContextOptions` constructor and an `OnModelCreating`** it does not have today — the class
  declares no constructor at all [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/MusicStoreEntities.cs:5-13]. Its one
  legacy directive [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/MusicStoreEntities.cs:1] substitutes cleanly, which
  is exactly what makes it the dangerous file: nothing about it looks like work, and the class-name
  connection-string convention it silently depends on stops meaning anything (section
  [4.5](#45-two-contexts-two-migration-sets-two-history-tables)).
- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs` stops being an initializer.** It becomes
  `Data/SeedData.cs`, shorn of the `DropCreateDatabaseIfModelChanges<MusicStoreEntities>` base type
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:9] that makes it destructive, and its `Seed` override
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:11-20] becomes the opt-in, fails-closed routine of
  section [5.4](#54-seeding--the-guard-fails-closed-on-three-checks). The row data survives — the same
  roughly 820 non-blank lines section 5.4 quotes, by the sizing method
  [08 §4.2](08-technical-debt-register.md) owns; the base class and the automatic invocation do not.
- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Order.cs` sheds a responsibility into a file that does not exist
  yet.** It loses `using System.Web.Mvc` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Order.cs:4] **and the
  class-level attribute that import exists to support**
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Order.cs:8]. Removing the import without removing the attribute does
  not compile; removing both without writing `Binding/CheckoutInputModel.cs` (section
  [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine)) removes the application's entire
  over-posting control at checkout. The entity itself stays at `Models/Order.cs`.

**Group C — five files where a substitution table is broadly right.** The five controllers other than
`AccountController`: `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/CheckoutController.cs`,
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/HomeController.cs`,
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs`,
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs` and
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs`. Namespace substitution, plus the
specific per-site work sections [4](#4-dependency-injection-and-object-lifetime) and
[13](#13-resolution-register--all-22-blockers-of-deliverable-12) assign — constructor injection, the
three `NotFound()` conversions [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:35],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:76],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:108], eager loading, the `Dispose`
deletion [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:125-128], the `AddToCart` verb
change and the JSON contract. **This is the only group the table below describes**, and it is five
files of twenty-seven.

```text
FROM: using System.Web.Mvc;                 TO: the target's MVC namespace
FROM: using System.Data.Entity;             TO: the target's EF Core namespace
FROM: using Microsoft.AspNet.Identity[.*];  TO: the target's Identity namespaces
FROM: using System.Web;                     TO: (removed; HttpContextBase becomes the framework's context type)
FROM: using System.Web.Optimization;        TO: (no successor; the file is deleted)
FROM: using Owin; / Microsoft.Owin.*;       TO: (no successor; the file is deleted or rewritten)
Applies in full to Group C's five files only. The same substitutions occur inside Group B, but there
they are a detail of a rewrite that changes the file's identity. Groups A and D are governed by
their role, not their imports.
```

**Group D — eight files where the work is explicit mapping or annotation rather than substitution.**
This is the group a substitution table declares finished, and **seven of the eight are not**. Seven of
them carry no legacy directive at all; the exception is `Models/Artist.cs`, whose lone
`using System.Web;` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Artist.cs:4] is unused template baggage — the class
declares two primitive properties [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Artist.cs:10-11] and names no
`System.Web` type — so that directive is deleted rather than substituted, which is why the file sits
here and not in Group C.

| File | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/ViewModels/ShoppingCartRemoveViewModel.cs` | **Gains explicit JSON property names** on all five properties [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/ViewModels/ShoppingCartRemoveViewModel.cs:5-9] — section [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy). Without them the cart page breaks silently, and this file carries not one legacy import |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/AccountViewModels.cs` | **Adapted** to the target Identity model shapes, and reduced by whatever the provider-driven removal of section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) makes unreachable |

| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Cart.cs` | Same explicit mapping; its `virtual Album` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Cart.cs:17] goes inert for the same reason, and its `[Key]` attribute [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Cart.cs:8] is the one convention override to carry across verbatim |

| `Models/AccountViewModels.cs` | **Adapted** to the target Identity model shapes, and **bounded** by the input maxima of section [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths). Nothing in it is dropped: `ExternalLoginConfirmationViewModel` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/AccountViewModels.cs:5-10] is retained with the surface (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types)), as are all four members of `ManageMessageId` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:374-380] |

The `virtual` modifiers on `Album.cs:30-32` and `Cart.cs:17` become inert — they were there for EF 6 proxy lazy loading, which the target does not do (section [4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy)) |

| `ViewModels/ShoppingCartRemoveViewModel.cs` | **Gains explicit JSON property names** on all five properties [:5-9] — section [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy). Without them the cart page breaks silently, and this file carries not one legacy import |
| `Models/AccountViewModels.cs` | **Adapted** to the target Identity model shapes. It is not reduced: section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) retains the external-login surface, so the external-login and manage view models it declares all remain in use, and it additionally **gains** the typed model that replaces the anonymous object passed to `_ExternalLoginsListPartial` (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) item (6)) |

The `virtual` modifiers on `Album.cs:30-32` and `Cart.cs:17` become inert — they were there for EF 6 proxy lazy loading, which the target does not do (section [4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy)) |

**So of the twenty-seven files: eight are deleted, six change identity, five take namespace
substitution plus per-site work, seven need explicit mapping or annotation, and exactly one ports
unchanged.** `8 + 6 + 5 + 7 + 1 = 27`, with no file counted twice — the last two figures are Group D's
eight split into the seven that need work and the one that does not. The import census cross-checks
the same way: the 19 files carrying at least one legacy directive are 7 of Group A's 8
(`Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` carries none), all 6 of Group B, all 5 of Group C and 1 of Group D
(`Models/Artist.cs`), and `7 + 6 + 5 + 1 = 19`. The census is how you find the files, not what you do
to them.

### 9.3 Two plan-correction records for the plan owner

Both items below are places where **this document's measurement of the checkout does not match the
frozen plan it is written against**. **Neither leaves an authority question open, because the plan
itself settles authority: its §0.11.3 states "Where a deliverable and the repository disagree, the
repository wins."** So the repository's measurement governs — inside this document and as the figure a
later reader should trust — and each item below is a **record notifying the plan owner** so the plan's
own text can be corrected at its next revision, not a question this document is waiting on. The plan
is frozen and **nothing here edits it**; its figure stands unaltered in the plan until its owner
changes it. Each item states the measured value, the plan's value, the delta, the cause, and the
disposition that follows from the rule.

**Item 1 — the authoritative `using System.Web;` file count is 11; the plan's value of 10 omits one
file.**

| Aspect | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| **Authoritative count, measured in this checkout** | **11** files — the value this document uses everywhere, reproducing command immediately below |
| **Plan value (§0.4.2 import census)** | 10 files, recorded here so the difference is on the record rather than in circulation |
| **Delta** | **Exactly one file: `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs`** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:4]. The plan's list is otherwise the measured set item for item, so the plan's 10 **is** the measured 11 minus that one entry |
| **Cause** | **A single-file omission from the plan's list, and not a method artifact.** The plan's list *includes* both files whose directive sits on line 1, [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1] and [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1], so it was not produced by a BOM-sensitive match: that form **misses exactly those two** and returns **9**, with a different set as well as a different total. No method that yields 10 on this checkout is known, and the difference is therefore an omission in the plan's enumeration rather than a disagreement about the source or an artifact of how it was counted. (BOM sensitivity is real and load-bearing elsewhere — it is what separates 17 from 19 in section [9.1](#91-the-census-and-how-to-count-it) — which is precisely why it should not be borrowed as the explanation here) |
| **Governing rule** | The plan's **§0.11.3**: "Where a deliverable and the repository disagree, the repository wins." The rule is the plan's own, so applying it is not a deviation from the plan — it is the plan's instruction for exactly this case |
| **Disposition** | **Settled, not pending.** 11 governs; the plan's 10 is superseded and is left untouched in the frozen plan, whose owner may fold the correction — the count and the addition of `Models/SampleData.cs` to the list — into its next revision. This entry is the notification that lets them do so. Nothing in this document's own arithmetic turns on it either way: the 19-of-27 census, the four-group partition of section [9.2](#92-the-four-groups) and the per-file dispositions are unaffected, because `Models/SampleData.cs` is in Group B on the strength of its `DropCreateDatabaseIfModelChanges` base class, not its imports |

The reproducing command is **not** `^`-anchored, because the anchor is what loses the two line-1
directives. `git grep` matches anywhere on the line, so the BOM is irrelevant to it, and the `grep -v`
filter excludes the `System.Web.*` directives that a substring match would otherwise pull in. Both
forms are printed, because the pair is the evidence that the anchored method is not the plan's:

```bash
git grep -n 'using System.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -v 'System\.Web\.'
# -> 11 lines, one per file:
#    App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1              Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:6
#    App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1              Global.asax.cs:4
#    App_Start/RouteConfig.cs:4               Models/Artist.cs:4
#    Controllers/AccountController.cs:6       Models/SampleData.cs:4
#    Controllers/HomeController.cs:3          Models/ShoppingCart.cs:4
#    Controllers/StoreController.cs:5
#
# The BOM-sensitive form, for contrast: 9 lines, not 10 and not 11. It drops
# App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1 and App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1 -- the two the plan's
# own list contains -- and it keeps Models/SampleData.cs:4, the one the plan omits.
# So its set is not the plan's set in either direction.
git grep -nE '^using System\.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | wc -l   # -> 9
git grep -nE '^using System\.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -cE 'SampleData'
# -> 1   (present in the anchored 9; absent from the plan's 10)
```

The eleven, each with its own locator:
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/RouteConfig.cs:4],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:6],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/HomeController.cs:3],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs:5],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:6],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Global.asax.cs:4], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Artist.cs:4],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:4] and
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:4].
