Row 70 does the same thing for the cookie's sliding renewal by minting a ticket with chosen timestamps. Neither needs a clock, a wait, or a change to the application's registrations — so the general rule this section now states is **a controllable clock, a constructible state, or a bounded wait, in that order of preference**, and a case that can name none of the three is a limit rather than a case |
| 3 | `RequiredUniqueChars = 4` in isolation | The four enabled complexity classes already force at least four distinct characters, so **no password exists** that fails this rule while passing rows 49a to 49d. There is no isolating case to write, and writing one that also fails another rule would prove nothing about this one | Nothing. It is a property of the policy, not a gap in the suite: row 49e covers it as an accepted boundary and this entry exists so that a reader does not read its absence as an omission |
| 4 | **Bounded, not unasserted.** The *exact* status code of the plaintext-to-HTTPS redirect | The enforcement point is the platform's and [06 §10.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns it, so a single code asserted here could contradict that decision. What is **no longer** left open is the admissible set: row 47 now asserts the status is one of exactly **`301`, `302`, `307`, `308`** — the four the two candidate enforcement points can produce, `301` from the platform's own HTTPS-only setting and `307` from `UseHttpsRedirection`'s default `RedirectStatusCode`, with `302` and `308` their temporary and permanent counterparts — together with the `Location`, host, scheme and empty-body assertions in that row. A `200`, a `4xx`, a `5xx`, a redirect to another host or back to `http` therefore **fails**, which is every materially wrong outcome | Its owner naming the enforcement point and its code. Row 47 then narrows the four-value set to that one literal, and nothing else in the row changes |
| 5 | **Bounded, not unasserted.** The *approved prose* of the cart-migration notice | The text is a product decision and a suite that hardcoded prose nobody has approved would fail on the day it is approved — which is why the earlier revision asserted only presence. That left the gap too wide: a notice reading `TODO` or carrying an exception message satisfied "non-empty and non-disclosing" on a technicality. So the mechanism changed rather than the ownership. The string lives in **one** place — a named entry in the application's committed resource file, `CartMigrationNotice`, which the view renders and **no** other site duplicates — and row 37 asserts the rendered text is **byte-equal to that entry's value**, so approving the text is a resource edit that keeps the suite green while any *other* text, including one substituted at runtime from an exception, fails. Row 37 additionally holds the entry's value itself to four predicates: non-empty after trimming, at least **20** characters, containing none of `TODO`, `TBD`, `FIXME`, `Lorem`, `placeholder`, `null`, `undefined`, `Exception`, `System.` or `SqlException`, and containing neither the account's login name nor the anonymous cart key nor any fixture `AlbumId` | The product owner approving the text, which is a change to the resource entry and to nothing in this suite. The four predicates and the byte-equality assertion stand either way |
| 6 | Rendered appearance, at every viewport and on every page | Asserted by nothing in section [12.4](#124-required-coverage), by design and with its reasoning stated in section [12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) | It is already closed, by the manual review section [12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) specifies and deliverable [07](07-effort-risks-sequencing.md) schedules. Listed here only so that this section is the single place a reader can see the full boundary of what the automated suite establishes |
| 7 | Performance, load and concurrency behaviour of any surface | No performance target exists to test against: the repository provides no baseline and no deliverable in this set sets one. A suite asserting an invented threshold would be asserting a requirement nobody wrote | A stated performance requirement with a measured baseline. The per-page query fan-out that [08 §5.2](08-technical-debt-register.md) records as F-08-03 is the surface that would need it first, and section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 29 is the closest thing the suite has — a **correctness** check on the aggregate's translation, explicitly not a performance one |
| 8 | **Open residual.** Functional behaviour of the scripted cart flow on **Edge, Firefox and Safari** — that is, on three of the four families [06 §10.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s matrix names | Section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 28 `28b` installs and drives **Chromium alone**, and section [12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual)'s manual review is about **rendering**, not about whether a handler fires. So the three families have neither automated nor manual **functional** evidence, and no wording in this document should be read as supplying it. It is listed as a **residual** rather than a defect because a one-engine functional suite is a defensible position — it is just not a decided one | An approval decision at [03](03-modernization-roadmap.md)'s **W1**, in the same decision set as the numbered deltas: **accept** the residual, recording the narrowed functional scope where [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) states the matrix; or **extend** Stage B to install the other engines and run `28b` under each, with [07](07-effort-risks-sequencing.md) sizing the three additional installs and the additional execution. Nothing in this suite changes under the first option and only the engine list changes under the second |

**Three limits this table previously carried are closed, and they are recorded here rather than silently
dropped.** Entry 2 above is the third, and it is the one worth reading twice: it was closed not by
acquiring a capability but by noticing that the assertion did not need one — a limit whose stated closure
mechanism is wrong stays open forever, because the thing it asks for never arrives. The other two were the
same defect on two headers: an assertion can only be as tight as the value its
owner publishes, and [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) published `Strict-Transport-Security`
and `Permissions-Policy` as *descriptions*. It now publishes both as **literals** — the max-age in seconds
with `includeSubDomains` and no `preload` token, and the four `Permissions-Policy` directives in a fixed
order — so section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 47 and row 45 assert **byte equality** against them
instead of a directive-presence check, and neither header's value is stated twice anywhere in the corpus.
The closure is worth a sentence because it is the mechanism this section exists for: a limit recorded with
what would close it is a limit somebody can close, and this is the case where somebody did.

**Nothing else in section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) is partial.** Every other behaviour, security
delta, approved delta, failure path and migration gate named anywhere in this document has a case in that
matrix or an entry above; the mapping is what the `Traces to` column carries, row by row, so a reader can
check the claim in either direction rather than taking it.

## 13. Resolution register — all 22 blockers of deliverable 12

This deliverable's acceptance criterion is that **every no-successor construct and every
differing-default item in deliverable 12 has a named resolution rather than a description.** This
section is the audit trail — the criterion is recorded in the requirement map at
[README](README.md). It
walks [12](12-migration-blockers.md)'s two groups in order. A row's *Resolution* column names the
decision; the *Where* column points at the section that specifies it.

### 13.3 The favourable findings, and where they are used

[12 §6](12-migration-blockers.md)'s four portability findings are consumed rather than restated:
`HttpContext.Current` appearing nowhere is why the service extraction of section
[4.8](#48-the-service-layer-and-the-two-patterns-deliberately-not-adopted) is a signature change rather
than an excavation; the dead `Controller` overload being provably unreferenced is why it is deleted
there with zero call-site impact; the absence of raw SQL anywhere is why section
[4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy) needs no SQL-dialect review; and the async
posture — no `.Result` and no `.Wait()` in any edition — is why the `TryUpdateModelAsync` conversion of
section [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine) has no sync-over-async debt behind
it.

### 13.4 The three transformations no tool infers

Called out separately because each is a **required step** rather than an observation, and none of them
is produced by any automated upgrade tool:

1. **The ten-versus-nine property fact of the checkout input model.** A tool reading the `[Bind]`
   attribute produces nine. Nine compiles, binds, persists, and silently disables the promo code —
   section [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine).
2. **The per-site lazy-loading decisions, including the one site that must *not* get an `Include`.** No
   tool can distinguish a client-side dereference from a navigation read inside a translated expression
   — section [4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy).
3. **The PascalCase JSON contract between one endpoint and one script.** No tool reads a JavaScript
   property access and infers a serializer constraint on a C# model — section
   [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy).

A fourth is worth the same status even though it is not a code transformation: **the authoritative
schema extraction gate** (sections [5.1](#51-domain-data-migration-starts-with-schema-extraction) and
[5.5](#55-the-identity-transition--a-schema-decision-plus-a-data-migration)). Every tool will happily
generate an initial migration; none will tell you it does not match the database your data is in.

## 14. Roll-up

### 14.1 The approach in eleven statements

1. **One composition root.** Twelve startup and configuration files collapse into `Program.cs` plus
   Razor and MSBuild conventions, with four different fates and no file's fate inferred from its
   imports.
2. **Nothing is applied at startup that changes a schema.** Migrations, seeding and administrator
   provisioning all leave the web application.
3. **Two contexts, one database, separate migration sets and history tables in one project.** The
   stores are coupled by convention, not by a foreign key; the consistency model is an explicit
   five-step ordering whose residual window is **not claimed closed** — the cart key is derived from
   the authenticated principal so no unauthenticated request can resolve it, and the next successful
   sign-in absorbs the reassignment idempotently. **And the cart itself is one concurrency domain, not
   four independent writers**: a concurrency token; **every mutation a single token-conditional statement
   whose affected-row count is asserted to be exactly one**, with the decrement-versus-delete decision
   re-taken on a fresh value rather than tested and then acted on; **the quantity bound inside that same
   statement, with a `CHECK` constraint behind it**; **a durable operation ledger** so a lost
   acknowledgement cannot double-apply; a checkout delete keyed on the rows it actually read; and a
   **discoverable, destination-indexed handoff** for the retired anonymous id — because a unique index
   constrains a pair and serializes nothing, and both of those columns have to be given a bounded length
   before any index over them can exist at all.
4. **Every silent-failure site is named individually.** Nine lazy-loading sites in three categories,
   one JSON contract, two `Dispose` overrides, one connection convention — resolved per site, not by
   policy.
5. **Query shape is a decision, not an afterthought.** Both unbounded list endpoints get a total
   ordering, a projection, a stated page size and a paging mechanism; the two — and only two —
   every-page components get a fixed query budget; the order write reads every price once; **the one
   browse predicate that is not a key gets a contract with two extraction-selected branches, neither of
   which loses a genre row**; and the provider carries an explicit retry, timeout, cancellation and async
   policy that the file-attached source never needed — **per command *and* per unit of work**, because
   the two differ by a product and only the second bounds a request.
6. **Data migration begins with a complete extraction and a schema diff that must pass**, and is
   performed by a named executor with defined idempotence, checkpointing and exit codes — **a run
   identity that is a parent row plus one independently fingerprinted row per store, and a durable
   lineage table the reconciling and sealing processes read rather than re-derive**, because they are
   separate processes from the load. An initial
   migration creates tables; it does not move rows and it cannot be trusted to match. **Acceptance is
   keyed sets and digests, not counts** — over a projection declared per class, so a target-only column
   is asserted against a named origin instead of quietly dropped from the comparison.
7. **The Identity transition preserves usernames as an invariant**, treats id preservation as an
   explicit convenience, aborts on normalized **username** and **role-name** collisions before writing,
   dispositions every table rather than only the users, verifies rather than assumes the
   password-hash format, and **configures the normalized columns' collation rather than inheriting one** —
   verified by target-side introspection, because those columns do not exist in the source for an
   extraction to report on.
8. **Policy is stated, not inherited.** Every authentication, cookie, password and lockout value is set
   explicitly and labelled preserved or hardening — including the two places this document deliberately
   declines to harden.
9. **Anti-forgery is global by default**, one state-changing `GET` becomes a `POST`, and the one
   form-less AJAX post gets a named header contract with three token tests.
10. **A single cutover, with two accepted costs and a rollback plan that states them in both
    directions.**
11. **Tests precede the port**, HTTP-level and semantic, against a two-database legacy baseline and a
    disposable SQL Server for the target — with rendered-appearance review scoped separately and
    manually.

### 14.2 What this document creates: nothing, and what the assessment nonetheless wrote

No **tracked** repository file was created, modified or deleted in producing it, other than this file,
and every target artifact named above is a specification for a separately approved implementation
phase. The qualifier is load-bearing: the assessment's restores and builds ran against this checkout
and left **eight ignored trees** in it — the `bin` and `obj` pairs of the three edition projects plus a
restored `packages` tree under `src/MVC4` and another under `src/MVC5` — which were removed, and whose
absence was then verified rather than assumed. Section
[1.4](#14-the-no-modification-constraint-and-the-boundary-that-makes-this-document-possible) carries
that account with the figures, and [10 §1.4](10-build-and-deployment-requirements.md) owns it.

So the closing check is the four-command one of section
[1.4](#14-the-no-modification-constraint-and-the-boundary-that-makes-this-document-possible), and it is
four rather than one because all eight trees were ignored on this checkout — `obj` by `[Oo]bj/`
[.gitignore:1], `bin` by `[Bb]in/` [.gitignore:2], and the two nested `packages` trees by `Packages/`
[.gitignore:33] rather than by the root-anchored `packages/*` [.gitignore:15], as section
[1.4](#14-the-no-modification-constraint-and-the-boundary-that-makes-this-document-possible) records
with its case dependency — and neither a bare status nor a tracked diff can see an ignored path:
`git diff --name-status ea2552d6eda7c20e9477a512e5c615665618cf35..HEAD` returns exactly thirteen `A`
rows, all under `docs/modernization/`, with no `M` or `D` row and no path outside it; and on a clean
checkout of that commit `git status --porcelain` is **empty**,
`git status --porcelain --ignored` is **empty** with no `!!` row, and `git clean -ndX` **lists
nothing**.

## Appendix A — Reproducibility

Every repository-wide claim in this document was produced by one of the commands below, run against
this checkout. They are collected here so each is re-runnable rather than merely cited.

```bash
# --- Section 1.3  The citation contract, checked mechanically -----------------
# Every citation carries a full repository-relative path and a locator that
# resolves in this checkout; no bare-locator shorthand is used anywhere.
# chr(96)*3 is the code-fence marker, spelled that way so this block can live
# inside a fence itself.
python - <<'PY'
import re, os
doc   = "docs/modernization/05-aspnet-core-migration-approach.md"
FENCE = chr(96) * 3
full     = re.compile(r"\[(src/[^\]]+?):(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?\]")
short    = re.compile(r"\[:[^\]]+\]")
pathonly = re.compile(r"\[src/[^\]:]+\]")
barefile = re.compile(r"\[[A-Za-z_][\w.\-]*\.(?:cs|cshtml|config|csproj|sln|sql|targets):[^\]]+\]")
infence = n = bad = nshort = npath = nbare = 0
for ln in open(doc, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines():
    if ln.lstrip().startswith(FENCE):
        infence ^= 1
        continue
    if infence:
        continue
    nshort += len(short.findall(ln))
    nbare  += len(barefile.findall(ln))
    npath  += len(pathonly.findall(ln))
    for m in full.finditer(ln):
        n += 1
        p, a = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
        b = int(m.group(3) or m.group(2))
        N = len(open(p, encoding="utf-8-sig").read().splitlines()) if os.path.exists(p) else -1
        if not (1 <= a <= b <= N):
            bad += 1
            print("UNRESOLVED", m.group(0))
print("full=%d shorthand=%d path-only=%d bare-filename=%d unresolved=%d"
      % (n, nshort, npath, nbare, bad))
PY
# -> full=496 shorthand=0 path-only=0 bare-filename=0 unresolved=0

python - <<'PY'
import subprocess, re
files = subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','*Web.Debug.config','*Web.Release.config'],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
tot = live = 0
for f in files:
    s = open(f, encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
    stripped = re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->', '', s, flags=re.S)
    n, m = len(re.findall(r'xdt:Transform', s)), len(re.findall(r'xdt:Transform', stripped))
    tot += n; live += m
    print('%-58s total=%d live=%d' % (f, n, m))
print('TOTAL=%d LIVE=%d' % (tot, live))
PY

python - <<'PY'
import subprocess, re
files = [f for f in subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','*.config'],
         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split() if '/packages/' not in f]
word = pre = close = live = 0
for f in files:
    s = open(f, encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
    stripped = re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->', '', s, flags=re.S)
    word  += len(re.findall(r'customErrors', s))

print('files=%d word=%d "<customErrors"=%d "</customErrors>"=%d live=%d'
      % (len(files), word, pre, close, live))

import subprocess, re
files = subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs'],

                 r'|Owin|Microsoft\.Owin|Microsoft\.AspNet\.Identity)\b')

print('files=%d  utf8-BOM=%d  naive=%d  bom_tolerant=%d' % (len(files), boms, naive, tol))
print('the 8 with no legacy directive:'); [print('  ', w) for w in without]

# --- Sections 1.4 / 14.2  The constraint this work was held to ----------------
# Four commands, not one, and they only mean anything together. Restores and
# builds ran against this checkout during the assessment and left eight ignored
# trees in it (527 files, 114,310,394 bytes); all eight were removed. All eight
# were ignored here, so the two commands a repository-state claim is usually
# rested on -- bare porcelain and the tracked diff -- reported a clean tree for
# the whole period those trees existed, and the two ignore-aware lines below are
# the ones that carry the claim. Which rule matched which path, per path:
git check-ignore --no-index -v src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/obj/x \
                               src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/bin/x src/MVC5/packages/x
# -> .gitignore:1:[Oo]bj/     src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/obj/x
#    .gitignore:2:[Bb]in/     src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/bin/x
#    .gitignore:33:Packages/  src/MVC5/packages/x
# --no-index makes the answer independent of tracking state. The three paths above
# are untracked, so the plain form reports the same rules; a TRACKED path is the
# case that differs -- plain check-ignore exits 1 for it with no output, because
# tracked files are not ignored, which is a different question from whether a rule
# matches. Verified both ways on a tracked path inside one of those trees:
git check-ignore -v src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/packages/repositories.config
# -> no output, exit 1  (tracked: suppressed, and no rule reported)
git check-ignore --no-index -v src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/packages/repositories.config
# -> .gitignore:33:Packages/  src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/packages/repositories.config
# The nested packages trees are matched by Packages/ (.gitignore:33), which has no
# interior separator and so matches at any depth, and NOT by packages/*
# (.gitignore:15), which has one and is therefore anchored to the repository root.
# The match is also case-dependent: it holds because core.ignorecase is true here.
git config core.ignorecase                                    # -> true
git -c core.ignorecase=false check-ignore --no-index -v src/MVC4/packages/x
# -> no output, exit 1: on a case-sensitive filesystem no rule ignores that tree
#
# And the four acceptance commands themselves:
git status --porcelain              # -> 0 lines, on a clean checkout of the commit
git status --porcelain --ignored    # -> 0 lines, and no '!!' row: nothing ignored exists
git clean -ndX                      # -> empty: no ignored artifact is present to remove
git diff --name-status ea2552d6eda7c20e9477a512e5c615665618cf35..HEAD
# -> exactly 13 rows, all "A", all under docs/modernization/:
#    01-architecture-overview.md  02-dependency-inventory.md

for d in src/MVC3/MvcMusicStore-Completed/MvcMusicStore/bin \
```
